notes: Lensfun/geometry can refuse GPU Micro Grain but CPU still works. Record route rather than marking that case skipped; use neutral geometry and lens off for an explicit GPU Micro control where needed.
summary: The driver times all three Denoise methods, but does not apply a recipe per method or establish that each actually changed the picture.
evidence: seed has no Denoise-specific branch and the method loop uses app defaults after resets. The single module ON/OFF screenshot signature goes through changeState, which hard-codes Clean Grain. The skip helper checks Edge colour but only enabled repairs and omits the frontend's other eligibility checks, including non-Bayer, incomplete Bayer cells and authored SDR. Explicit nonzero defaults and all three selectors are wired, but visible changes per method are not statically verified. The method loop times its own eye after enabling and dragging, so that eye measures OFF only. Cold Clean Grain can already have been primed by earlier modules in --all.
proposed_fix: On IMG_0790.CR2, seed and hash exact per-method control maps; use the same maps on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW. Clean Grain: {method:'clean_grain',amount:0.90,luminance:0.85,color_noise:0.90,detail_recovery:0.35,finest_noise:0.75,fine_noise:0.70,medium_noise:0.65,coarse_noise:0.60,grain_evenness:1,color_splotches:1,clean_splotches:true,clean_fringes:true,protect_color_edges:false,splotch_size:'small'}. Simple: {method:'standard',amount:0.90,luminance:0.85,color_noise:0.90,detail_recovery:0.35,finest_noise:0.75,fine_noise:0.70,medium_noise:0.65,coarse_noise:0.60}. Micro Grain: {method:'micro_grain',micro_luminance:0.85,micro_color:0.85,micro_detail:0.35}. Start each OFF, apply just that map, then compare settled ON and OFF signatures separately before timing. Use microGrainUnavailable(current lane) for skipped rows. Add separately timed, primed ON and OFF for every eligible method, and label a cold run cold only when measured preparation is initially absent.
check: H3 and noisy-photo Fit plus large 100%: assert each eligible method changes pixels against its own OFF control, record no_op per failed method, and retain the default Clean Grain recipe for cross-module probes. Also switch Clean Grain → Simple → Micro Grain → Clean Grain without changing view, waiting for the current selected method each time, then compare with a fresh execution of each recipe.

notes: Phase 2 owns the findings file only; prepare the output-changing patch in Phase 4.
summary: At native zoom, a cached GPU Micro Grain tile can keep showing the previous slider settings.
evidence: The Micro tile cache key contains fitKey, frame size, working space and region but not microLuminance, microColor or microDetail. The hit copies final resolved pixels and returns before writeMicroGrainRegion. setDenoiseControls replaces the controls without dropping tiles; the same Micro fitKey survives live changes. The Fit reduced key does include all three sliders.
proposed_fix: Add all three Micro controls to the final RGB tile key, leaving reusable Bayer and demosaic keys unchanged.
check: Large 100% and eligible GPU Micro source: warm a visible tile, move one Micro control without panning, require a changed exact signature and match a fresh render at the new value.

notes: Phase 2 owns the findings file only; prepare the output-changing patch in Phase 4.
summary: At native zoom, GPU Clean Grain can reuse an old colour correction after settings change, even across a packed-colour to brightness-only layout change.
evidence: The bounded Clean Grain tile key uses fitKey instead of the computed fineGrainPixelControls endpoint key. The fit only includes a subset of controls (amount, luminance, recovery, fine and medium bands and whether a fit is required), not splotch reach, fringe/edge protection, colorNoise, coarse/finest bands or the actual grainEvenness value. An existing denoiseTile hit only checks width and height, so it can return pixels from the old settings or an incompatible rgba32uint versus rgba16float endpoint texture. Fit's reducedGrainKey already uses endpoint controls.
proposed_fix: Include fineGrainPixelControls(controls,true) and the packed layout in bounded Clean Grain tile identity; keep blend-only Color Splotches (and evenness only where truly represented by the endpoints) out of the key.
check: At 100% with GPU Clean Grain, warm the same tile and switch Small to Large, toggle edge/fringe protection and edit Color Noise. Exact pixels must track the selected controls and equal a fresh render; also cover packed to unpacked.

felt_impact: Potentially seconds to tens of seconds of whole wait when a 100% toggle falls off the viewport path; near zero on an existing whole-source hit. Audit cold.denoise.micro_grain.toggle_on and own.denoise.micro_grain.eye at large 100%, lens Auto applied versus Off, then a separate CPU spatial/HDR-ceiling repro.
notes: Full-photo render is required in some cases by design. Do not claim the 25 s is fully avoidable or count previously documented costs as a new regression.
summary: Lens-corrected Micro Grain can turn a native-zoom toggle into a whole-photo CPU job.
evidence: prepare_micro returns 422 when Lensfun actually applied; non-neutral geometry also refuses the GPU. The CPU viewport path rejects spatial grade, resampled geometry or a live highlight ceiling, then main._micro_preview_raw falls through to the whole native Micro render and reduction. A 50 MP RGB float32 render is about 600 MB alongside the existing developed RGB, about 100 MB of Bayer samples, tile workspaces and possibly a disk-backed lens output. The historical Mac 78% Lensfun run spent about 25 s of 53–55 s in Micro rendering alone. The cached CPU source is independent of exposure/contrast/film, so only a cache miss incurs the native build.
proposed_fix: First isolate which refusal dominates. For an already-eligible viewport keep and reuse its exact native tiles/source across eye changes. For full-frame-only cases, investigate an exact bounded reduction from tiles rather than materializing a second native RGB frame; do not remove whole-frame guarantees or start a lens GPU port from this audit.
check: Mac 8 GB, report route, micro_render_ms and whole wait with footprint on large RAW. Compare the exact finished picture to the existing route before taking a change.

felt_impact: Zero on a cache hit, potentially several seconds on a large cache miss. Audit probe.denoise.toggle_on with Film and Detail ON/OFF at large Fit; compare grain_reduced_cache hit/miss, resize time and eviction reasons, not just denoiseRebuilds.
summary: Warm Clean Grain can lose its expensive exact Fit picture during the Off half of an A/B toggle.
evidence: Off retains the selector and its fit but turns selected to original. Memory reclaim only identifies the matching reduced Grain texture as active when selected is resolved. A normal inactive entry is eligible for reclamation, as are older entries under pressure. A miss in ensureFineGrainReduced reruns native fetch, Denoise passes and resize in strips even with a fit-cache hit and zero selector rebuilds. The eye keeps the outgoing picture until the exact result. The entry is 16 bytes per Fit pixel; at a 4096×2731 Fit tier that is about 179 MB retained.
proposed_fix: If re-audit attributes slow warm toggles to this, prefer one matching exact reduced picture over older entries during ordinary eye-Off reuse while retaining existing pressure and admission limits.
check: Prime large Fit, toggle off, apply controlled pressure and toggle back on. Verify cache retention when affordable, original exact picture, and intact safety eviction at higher pressure.

felt_impact: Zero after preparation has settled. On a real overlap, the gain is up to the already spent attempt, from a model round trip to seconds of large fit work. Audit cold.denoise.clean_grain.toggle_on at large Fit with a separate controlled overlapping probe.tone.exposure / probe.tone.contrast commit; standard Phase 3 serial priming will not reproduce it on its own.
summary: A downstream Grade edit can restart preparation already in flight even though it does not invalidate settled preparation.
evidence: The settled selector and fit keys depend on source, rendition, tier, geometry, repair generation and Denoise inputs, not Tone, Film or Detail. However recalculateDenoiseAnalysis restarts whenever editRevision changes, and the model GET/POST transport checks that same global edit revision. A Tone drag acknowledgement can discard strip work or reject a model publication even when backend source_identity and geometry are unchanged. JS measurement acquire keys the full URL including the revision and does not stop a measurement that has already entered measure until it finishes.
proposed_fix: Give Denoise preparation an input-specific ownership token covering source epoch, repair generation, rendition, geometry, scale, Denoise controls and refresh; preserve final presentation's latest-grade check.
check: Commit Exposure, Contrast, Detail or Film mid-fit and assert one preparation completes and the latest grade displays. Repeat with a real source/geometry change and require cancellation.

felt_impact: Likely tens of milliseconds on cache-hit large Fit edits and warm toggles, plus lower allocation churn and pressure when they coincide. Audit probe.tone.exposure, probe.tone.contrast and probe.denoise.toggle_on with Denoise ON at large Fit, and log blend dispatch and peak bytes.
summary: A hit on exact Clean Grain at Fit still allocates and computes a full blend texture on every draw, including unrelated Grade updates.
evidence: ensureFineGrainReduced retains packed endpoints but renderTo always calls blendReducedCleanGrain while Color Splotches is unchanged, with a fresh rgba16float output and separate queue submission; the render finally destroys the blend. A 4096×2731 Fit tier allocates about 89 MB per draw just for this output, in addition to the approximately 179 MB endpoints. At 50 MP one full-frame RGBA16F or float32 RGB image would be 400 MB or 600 MB respectively; do not assume those are allocated on the bounded Fit path.
proposed_fix: Reuse one blended source keyed on endpoint texture identity and strength under the existing allocator, evicting it before endpoints, or consume the same quantized blend directly where supported. Measure retained memory versus churn before choosing.
check: Hit the same Fit endpoints and strength across repeated Exposure/Contrast edits and eye cycles. Require identical pixels, zero repeated blend dispatches on the warm route, and no budget regression.

felt_impact: Expected tens to low hundreds of milliseconds for a first warm large Simple 100% toggle if the visible tiles are admitted; smaller when CPU-prepared packed tiles already hit. Audit own.denoise.standard.eye plus a dedicated warm toggle-on sample at large 100%; inspect actual tile hits/resolves.
summary: The first settled native render of a Simple or CPU-backed Denoise state deliberately leaves nothing in the resolved tile cache.
evidence: denoiseTilePrefix is null on the first non-endpoint, non-Micro state, so denoiseInto reconstructs even on the second render: only then can it populate the cache. The guard avoids filling tiles for every transient slider step but also excludes an exact settled or priming pass. Separate CPU-prepared packed tiles may already be retained; the repeated work is the resolved-frame tile copy/blend, not necessarily the CPU wavelet.
proposed_fix: Let an exact settled render seed only admitted visible tiles, while keeping the second-pass guard for transient, measurement and noise-view renders.
check: First exact ON, then OFF, then ON at same native viewport and settings. Check tile resolves drop and resulting pixels are identical.

felt_impact: Likely tens of milliseconds on ordinary cold GPU measurement; potentially more if removing 16 MiB of live demand prevents a measured CPU fallback. Audit cold.denoise.standard.toggle_on and cold.denoise.clean_grain.toggle_on on the first large/noisy source, logging noise_measurement_cpu_fallback and measured allocation.
summary: Cold GPU noise measurement keeps a full input buffer after its only dispatch and uses a separate command submission for each pass.
evidence: The full window set is 16×256×256 RGBA float32, or 16 MiB per buffer. The memory gate requires about 136 MiB for eight full buffers plus overhead and can send measurement to the CPU when Grade headroom is narrow. input is only used by the first conversion and could back an equivalently sized later scratch role. dispatch constructs and submits its own encoder even between GPU-only dependencies; host readbacks are the actual batch boundaries.
proposed_fix: Reuse input storage as a later non-overlapping scratch buffer and batch GPU-only chains between mapped reads in submission order. Do not change sample windows, reductions, measurement identities or policy budgets.
check: Compare complete measurement model values and rendered pixels to the current GPU path, instrument submission count and memory at the 1 MP window cap. Measurement is shared with export/Proof.

notes: Changing route changes the visible status and can change pixels within tolerance, so ask Steve in Phase 4. No patch written in read-only Phase 2.
summary: Micro Grain stays latched to the CPU after undoing the geometry that made the GPU route unsupported.
evidence: The geometry refusal in analyzeAdaptiveDenoise is permanent and keyed on the rejected geometry. runtime.microBackup keeps that old key; both renderGpuDraftInner and recalculateDenoiseForView test canRun on the old latch before computing a key for the now-neutral geometry. Ordinary geometry/Undo does not clear this backup, and loadDenoiseDocument preserves it within the same session/method. Selecting a different method clears it.
proposed_fix: Before enforcing the Micro backup, compare its source eligibility identity against the current source/geometry/repair identity and clear stale failure ownership. Preserve the latch for the same inputs and for a genuinely unavailable GPU.
check: Eligible GPU Micro with lens off, add a crop, let CPU settle, undo the crop. Expect GPU again without a method switch and check preview agreement.

summary: The audit can mislabel warm Denoise rebuilds and can time out on an accepted reduced CPU fallback.
evidence: analysisCalls increments before cache lookups, so a setup call with a fit hit counts as a rebuild. Conversely, an expensive exact Fit reduction miss or Bounded CPU source miss can happen without analysisCalls changing. The POST filter later only counts analysis/prepare URL strings, not denoise-measurement, denoise-grain or CPU preview requests, and the Tone probes do not accumulate rebuilds. stable also requires the exact requested processing edge, excluding a legitimate bounded CPU result at 4096 if the native request was larger.
proposed_fix: Count selector setup, fit misses, exact reduced misses and CPU preparation misses separately, including Tone probes while Denoise is on. Track an explicitly accepted reduced fallback with actual edge and reason as a separate route/sample, not a successful full-resolution timing.
check: Force one cache hit, one reduced miss and one reduced CPU route in the harness calibration; verify the counters, route, exactness and recorded dimensions match the action.

felt_impact: One settings round trip (likely tens of milliseconds when idle, longer behind a queued edit), zero gain if rendering needs a synchronized backend source request. Audit probe.denoise.toggle_on versus toggle_off with Tone or Film ON at typical Fit and log click-to-save-ack versus save-ack-to-first-render separately.
summary: Warm toggle-on waits for the settings save before it looks for a ready GPU result.
evidence: Toggle-off starts its exact GPU draw alongside persistDenoiseSettings; toggle-on waits for the serialized edit command to complete before checking selector identity, then starts the exact draw. If another Grade commit is queued, the click inherits that wait even on a full prepared cache hit.
proposed_fix: If the save wait is material, test overlapping only a GPU draw whose exact source and preparation are already resident, keeping owner/generation checks and requiring a successful save for final acceptance. Keep the save-first path where backend assets must be fetched.
check: An unchanged warm Fit pair should retain identical frames. Then force a delayed or failed edit acknowledgement and verify no wrong-lane, superseded or unsaved frame is accepted.
